title: The Formula to Great Fried Rice with Any Ingredients
summary: America's Test Kitchen presents a practical, universal approach to fried rice, codifying a core formula that works with a wide range of ingredients and styles. The video walks through rice preparation (emphasizing the use of stale rice for optimal grain separation, with alternatives for fresh rice and brown rice), a flexible mix-ins plan (eggs plus any proteins and vegetables), and a step-by-step cooking order using a wok. Key techniques include preheating a carbon steel wok, cooking ingredients sequentially to maintain texture and flavor, using fats to carry aromatics, salting at strategic moments, and finishing with optional additions like water to loosen stubborn rice clumps. The host demonstrates practical pacing, mise en place, and seasoning strategy, concluding with garnishes and a reminder that the rice-to-mix-ins ratio should emphasize the grain for the signature fried-rice texture.
topics: mise en place and landing zone
preheating a wok to wisps of smoke
adding water to break up clumps

sections.title: Intro
sections.description: Introduces the idea that fried rice follows a universal formula and highlights the importance of rice prep. Discusses using stale leftover rice, retrogradation, and how fridge storage accelerates staling. Covers options for making rice less sticky (baking-sheet cooling, fridge chilling ~30 minutes) and mentions brown rice as a slower-cooking alternative that still yields non-sticky grains.

featured_techniques.technique: Use stale rice and retrogradation to achieve drier, separable grains for fried rice
Spread freshly cooked rice on a rimmed baking sheet and chill, then cook in the fridge for about 30 minutes to maximize surface area and moisture evaporation
Consider brown rice as an alternative; bran layer slows water absorption and reduces stickiness
Dice vegetables uniformly (roughly 1/4–1/2 inch) to ensure even cooking and consistent bites
Separate scallion whites and greens for distinct roles in flavoring and finishing
Salt eggs early to denature proteins, producing a looser, more blendable scramble
Preheat the wok until wisps of smoke to ensure fast, high-heat cooking and clean toss
Cook mix-ins individually to control doneness and seasoning, then combine with the rice
Use water as a lubricant to break up clumps if rice sticks together, then cook off moisture
Let rice come to room temperature before frying to ease clump-breaking and achieve a better fry
Aim for a rice-to-mix-in ratio of roughly 2:1 to keep rice as the dominant texture
Finish with optional garnishes (chili crisp, herbs, sesame) to create bite-by-bite variation
